reason: Compares definitions of individual, marginal, component and undiversified VaR; correct entry is component VaR as a partition summing to portfolio VaR.
Diversification benefit as undiversified minus diversified VaR for a three-asset portfolio at 95%.
Reading undiversified VaR for a long/short book: it is the worst case at correlation of minus one, not plus one.
Individual VaR with absolute position and component VaR keeping the sign for a short leg, via individual VaR times rho.
Marginal VaR of one asset computed from covariance matrix and positions, alpha times (Sigma x)_i over sigma_p W.
Statements on marginal VaR being unitless, equal to (VaR/W) times beta, and its sign and derivation.
Incremental VaR of a multi-factor trade using the marginal VaR shortcut, sum of marginal VaR times exposure change.
Marginal VaR shortcut applied to a large trade; full before-and-after revaluation is needed because VaR changes nonlinearly.
Component VaR (tangent) versus exact reduction from deleting a position (curve) in a two-position book.
Percent contribution of a negatively correlated asset via component VaR equals individual VaR times rho over portfolio VaR.
Component VaR properties: sums to portfolio VaR, equals individual VaR times rho, linear approximation quality, not individual-VaR shares.
Simulation-based component VaR from averaged conditional P&L; the brief excludes simulation-based component VaR from selectors.
Tangent versus curve chart: component VaR along the tangent against incremental VaR of deletion along the curve.
General rationale for reporting marginal VaR next to individual VaR; no specific allocation calculation or rule is tested.
Choose position to cut using betas (highest beta, volatility and weight distract) and compute VaR reduction as (VaR/W) times beta times amount.
Fully invested switch: cut highest marginal VaR, add to lowest, compute first-order VaR reduction.
Equal marginal VaRs (equal betas) mean the minimum-risk allocation is reached; not the return-to-risk optimum.
Negative marginal VaR on a short leg versus its positive component VaR; stem built around confusing marginal sign with hedging.
Shortcut incremental VaR of a client trade, marginal VaR times added position, to judge whether it lowers VaR.
Incremental VaR of a multi-leg rebalancing via the marginal VaR shortcut, with individual VaR as distractor.
Marginal VaR times size used as precise estimate for liquidating a 45% holding; shortcut is only for small changes.
Choose which sleeve to cut by highest marginal VaR, not largest component VaR, and compute resulting VaR.
Compute marginal VaRs from volatilities, correlation and positions, then shift from higher to lower marginal VaR.
Choose the new asset to add with the smallest marginal VaR (alpha rho sigma) and compute the incremental VaR.
Risk-minimizing two-asset weight where marginal VaRs are equal, and the common marginal VaR.
